mcat_description.short: Telecom shelters are prefabricated, thermally insulated enclosures built from PUF (polyurethane foam) sandwich panels on a steel frame, designed to house BTS equipment, batteries, power systems, and MW racks at telecom tower sites.
mcat_description.long: Telecom shelters are factory-assembled, portable cabins constructed using pre-painted galvanised (PPGI) steel sheet skins with CFC-free polyurethane foam cores (typically 50–80mm thick), providing thermal insulation, weatherproofing, and structural rigidity for housing sensitive telecom equipment in outdoor environments. The floor assembly typically comprises a PUF-insulated sandwich panel topped with 19mm marine plywood and a 2mm antistatic floor mat, while doors feature three-point locking systems and aluminium-channel frames. In India, shelters must comply with TEC Generic Requirements (TEC-GR-RS-BSH) issued by the Department of Telecommunications, and are designed to withstand ambient temperatures from -30°C to +70°C, humidity up to 95%, and wind speeds up to 200 km/h. Variants include standard BTS shelters, green/energy-efficient shelters with passive phase-change thermal management, knock-down (KD) shelters for remote deployment, and larger multi-compartment enclosures for railway and utility applications.

market_context: Telecom shelters in India are governed by TEC Generic Requirements (TEC-GR-RS-BSH-001-02) issued by the Department of Telecommunications (DOT), making TEC approval a mandatory certification signal for buyers procuring for licensed telecom operators. The dominant construction standard uses PPGI (pre-painted galvanised iron) sheet skins with CFC-free PUF cores at 50–80mm thickness and 40 kg/m³ foam density, confirmed across multiple Indian manufacturers. A significant and growing sub-segment is the 'Green Telecom Shelter' — energy-efficient variants using passive phase-change materials (PCM) to reduce air-conditioning dependency, driven by telecom operators' energy cost reduction mandates. Manufacturers are concentrated in NCR (Faridabad, Greater Noida, Noida), Bengaluru, Ahmedabad, and Mumbai, with pan-India supply capability. Railway telecom shelters represent a distinct institutional buyer segment with larger multi-compartment enclosures (up to 5m x 15m) supplied to Indian Railways. IP protection ratings (IP54 to IP65) and wind resistance (up to 200 km/h) are key technical differentiators cited by multiple manufacturers.
